notEstablished.revitalisation: Not established from the sources consulted. The Advisory Committee's Fifth Opinion on Liechtenstein (ACFC, adopted 1 February 2021) records that on depositing its instrument of ratification Liechtenstein declared that no national minorities in the sense of the Framework Convention exist in its territory, and that it made a similar declaration on ratifying the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages; the Opinion describes anti-discrimination, hate-speech and integration measures but no language revitalisation or language-promotion measure, no body running one, no start date and no funding. Eurydice's Key data on teaching languages at school in Europe (2023 edition, policy position 2021/22) lists German as Liechtenstein's only state language on Figure A1 with no regional or minority language of official status, and the report describes no promotion measure for Liechtenstein anywhere in its text. Neither document addresses any measure for German itself.
